drafts.angle: Risk first: order by what is least known. The six things that could be a class bigger than estimated or show Alpha is not reachable (a desktop build of the game Orb actually plays, the first real Steam Deck run, the beam rework, the gravity well, the horde, the move table) are each built or sized by a throwaway trial in A1 or A2, before weeks are committed to work that depends on them. Early milestones are heavy and unglamorous; the first build with new things to press is A3; in exchange the path's length is known from evidence by the end of A2.
drafts.pace: About 35M tokens of finished director work a week (range 25M to 50M): roughly 60 to 80% of the weekly allowance, directors mostly on the cheaper models (about 1 meter point per 1M tokens, 1.6 on the largest), about a third of each week going to the Executive Producer's briefs, reviews, gates and rework. The record is thin (no clean weekly figures), so weeks are ranges; A-PROCESS-08 (a weekly token record) is in A1 to tighten them. Token budgets are size classes (S 0.25M, M 1.2M, L 4M, XL 8M) with no comparables. People's time is added: Orb plays each build (2 to 4 days), one Deck friend at A2, two at A6.

drafts.critical_path: A-PROCESS-03 (commit the working tree) -> A-CODE-03 and the ten switch groups A-CODE-01 needs -> A-CODE-01 -> A-CODE-02 (golden record for the played game) -> A-TOOLS-01 (one-command desktop build, also needs A-LEGAL-02) -> A-ENERGY-02 (model page) -> A-ENERGY-01 + A-COMBAT-02 in GW2 -> A-COMBAT-04 (move table, with A-COMBAT-06 beside it) in GW3 -> tuning A-AI-02, A-QA-05, A-QA-08 in GW4 -> the candidate's soak and bands and two friends' Deck sessions (X-01). Near-critical beside it: A-TOOLS-01 -> A-TOOLS-02 -> A-QA-01 -> X-01; and A-MODES-01 -> A-MODES-02 -> A-AI-01 -> A-QA-06. The safety chain (A-LEGAL-01, A-LEGAL-08 -> A-LEGAL-03 -> A-PERF-01 on a real Deck) gates the Deck's answer, so it is placed second.
risks: Main cannot simply be made into the game Orb plays: 72 of 92 switch rows differ, patches exist only in a preview tool, the golden record is valid only with switches off, and gates have never run on the played configuration (the readings on the globe ground already fail). If A1 takes three weeks instead of one and a half, everything moves by the difference. Guard: land row by row with a gate run each; nothing from A3 lands until GW1 closes.

The Steam Deck says no to something: a shader the driver rejects, a frame rate well under 30, text too small at 1280 by 800, or the Deck's controls not arriving as a pad. Guard: a CI job that makes the Linux build draw one still in A1, the real session in A2, a bench file from the same friend at A3 and A4, the Deck's default quality built at A5 from real numbers.

The fight rework is a class bigger than estimated: beam, signature inputs, stamina loop and gravity well all change the same exchange code in one window, and the beam struggle and the computer's beam play hang off the old beam. Guard: spikes S1 and S2 before it starts, each piece behind its own switch with its own probe, and a stop rule (if the well's first cut is not playable at A3's midpoint, A3 ships size and zones and the snap moves to GW3).

drafts.critical_path: Two chains; the longer wins. (1) The fight chain, set by tokens: A-CODE-01 (main becomes the played game, golden window 1) -> A-ENERGY-02 (the model page) -> A-ENERGY-01 (stamina, energy and body loop) and A-COMBAT-02 (signatures on Orb's inputs) -> A-COMBAT-04 (move table) -> A-CONTROLS-06 (the coverage probe that proves X-03) -> tuning inside golden window 3 -> the candidate; beside it A-COMBAT-03 (the gravity well), the largest single row, waiting on Orb's answer about whose stick moves whom up close. About 8 to 11 weeks of work from A1's close. (2) The newcomer chain, set by people: A-LEGAL-01 and A-LEGAL-08 -> A-LEGAL-03 (gate list green) -> A-LEGAL-02 and A-TOOLS-01 (a desktop build can be made) -> A-PERF-01 (a Linux build draws on a real Deck) -> A-TOOLS-02, A-TOOLS-05, A-LEGAL-05 -> A-QA-01 (guide and checklist) -> tester round 1 -> tester round 2 on the candidate (X-01). Shorter in tokens, but with two waits on volunteers no budget shortens.
risks: The outside-tester gate list does not go green on the globe ground in A1 (A-LEGAL-01, A-LEGAL-08, A-CAMERA-02): until it does no outside tester may play anything and A2 cannot hand out a build.

The Linux build does not hold up on a real Steam Deck (A-PERF-01): it has never drawn a picture, the shaders have never run on the Deck's driver and the frame rate is unknown; this path meets the risk at A2 on purpose instead of at the candidate.

The fight window grows: golden window 3 holds 1 XL and 7 L rows with no comparables (gravity well, beam rewrite, stamina loop, signatures, move table) in the area where Orb's workshop ideas arrive fastest; guarded by change control, early decisions and starting behind switches in A2 and A3.

X-03's probe (A-CONTROLS-06) lands with the move table (A-COMBAT-04) in every draft because the register says it needs it; no draft questions that dependency, though a cell-pressing probe could be written against today's table.
A-CODE-01 and its ten needed rows share one milestone in all three (43 to 47 needs links sit inside single milestones); none gives the order inside A1, where the first risk lives.
Size classes have no comparables, yet all three give totals to a decimal place; A-PROCESS-08 is in A1 everywhere but no draft names the date the weeks are re-estimated.
The year-end holidays are in no range; every range runs through late December (only modes notes the omission).
The first two-hour soak on a real Deck, the horde's largest wave on a Deck, and five LAN 2v2 matches are each first passed at or one milestone before the candidate.
No milestone says what happens if its exit is missed (slip, cut or ship short); risk has one stop rule, the others none.

Directors' load is not checked: each lists who is active but none adds up a director's rows per milestone against what one session lands in a week.
